drills.q: Conjugate 'to be' for 'he': He ___ a teacher.
drills.hint: 'be' is irregular: I am, you are, he/she/it is.

drills.q: Conjugate 'to have' for 'she': She ___ two cats.
drills.hint: Only he/she/it changes 'have' to 'has'.

drills.q: Past simple of 'to go': Yesterday I ___ to work.
drills.hint: 'go' is irregular; its past is 'went', not 'goed'.

drills.q: Present simple of 'to do' for 'it': It ___ not matter.
drills.hint: he/she/it takes 'does'; also used to form questions.

drills.q: Past participle of 'to eat': I have ___ lunch.
drills.hint: eat → ate (past) → eaten (past participle), used after 'have'.

drills.q: Add -ing to 'to run': They are ___.
drills.hint: Double the final consonant after a single vowel: run → running.

drills.q: 'a happy feeling' in one word?
drills.hint: Opposite of 'sad'.

drills.q: What do you call the room where you cook?
drills.hint: You prepare and cook food there.

drills.q: The English word for the female parent?
drills.hint: Casual forms: 'mum' (UK), 'mom' (US).

drills.q: What is the opposite of 'expensive'?
drills.hint: It means costing very little.

drills.q: The English word for a device you use to make calls?
drills.hint: Short for 'telephone'.

drills.q: Choose the article: I saw ___ elephant. (a/an)
drills.hint: Use 'an' before a vowel sound; 'elephant' starts with one.

drills.q: Comparative of 'good': This one is ___ than that.
drills.hint: 'good' is irregular: good → better → best.

drills.q: Make it negative: 'She works here.' → She ___ work here.
drills.hint: Use doesn't + base verb; the -s moves to the auxiliary.

drills.q: Plural of 'child'?
drills.hint: An irregular plural, not 'childs'.

drills.q: Write the number 15 as a word.
drills.hint: Note 'fif', not 'five', plus '-teen'.

drills.q: How do you say the time 8:45 using 'to'?
drills.hint: 'to' counts the minutes before the next hour.

drills.q: How do you politely greet someone before noon?
drills.hint: Switch to 'Good afternoon' after 12pm.

drills.q: What phrase do you say to ask for the restaurant bill politely?
drills.hint: Americans say 'the check, please'.

drills.q: How do you reply to 'Thank you'?
drills.hint: A standard, polite response to thanks.
